component.name: Apache Unomi
component.description: Java reference implementation of the OASIS Context Server (CXS) spec, a Customer Data Platform. It collects behavioural events about visitors (typically from a browser via the unomi-tracker JavaScript over a public context endpoint), builds and stores profiles and segments, evaluates rules and conditions, exposes REST and GraphQL APIs, and persists to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. Runs in an Apache Karaf/OSGi container. The threat model is a v0 draft by the ASF Security team pending Unomi PMC ratification; many statements are marked inferred.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document (draft v0); this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Unomi context server deployment
blueprints.description: Architecture described by the Unomi threat model: browsers post events unauthenticated to the public context endpoint; authenticated integrators use the REST/GraphQL admin APIs to author conditions, rules, segments, and scopes; the rule/condition engine evaluates expressions; data persists to an operator-secured Elasticsearch/OpenSearch backend.

assets.name: Public context ingestion endpoint
assets.description: /context.json and /eventcollector (EventsCollectorServlet): unauthenticated, internet-facing by design, the highest-value untrusted surface. Its gate is JSON-Schema validation plus the public-event allow-list (protected events / third-party server key mechanism), not authentication.

assets.name: Rule / condition / segment engine and scripting
assets.description: Services and scripting modules evaluating MVEL/OGNL expressions; historically the RCE surface (CVE-2020-11975, CVE-2020-13942, CVE-2021-31164), since constrained so that public input cannot reach expression evaluation.

assets.name: REST and GraphQL admin APIs
assets.description: Authenticated surface where conditions, rules, segments, and scopes are defined; assumed not exposed to the public network and trusted to the credential's authority.

assets.name: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch persistence
assets.description: Profile, segment, and event storage via persistence-elasticsearch / persistence-opensearch; Unomi's use of it is in model, the backend's own security is the operator's.

zones.name: Public web clients
zones.description: Browsers running unomi-tracker on the open internet, hitting the public context endpoint unauthenticated.

zones.name: Authenticated integrators and admins
zones.description: API clients and operators authoring conditions, rules, segments, and scopes; trusted to their credential's authority, with the operator fully trusted.

zones.name: Unomi server
zones.description: The Unomi process in its Karaf/OSGi container: ingestion servlets, rule engine, schema validation, admin APIs.

zones.name: Search backend
zones.description: Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, assumed deployed on a trusted network and secured by the operator.

persona.description: A browser running unomi-tracker, hitting the public context endpoint unauthenticated from the open internet; the primary untrusted actor.
Calls the REST/GraphQL APIs authenticated; may author conditions, rules, segments, and scopes. Trusted to its credential's authority.
Controls configuration, the Karaf container, plugins, and the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch backend. Trusted.
Another Unomi node in the same deployment.

assumptions.description: The public context endpoint is internet-facing by design (browsers post events directly); the admin REST/GraphQL APIs are assumed not public and authenticated.
The Elasticsearch/OpenSearch backend is deployed on a trusted network and secured by the operator.
Attackers who already control the host, the Karaf container, the config, the plugins, or the search backend are out of model (operator-trusted).
unomi-site, samples/, and itests/ are not production trust surfaces; unomi-tracker is a client-side satellite of this model.

threats.name: Public input reaching OGNL/MVEL expression evaluation (RCE)
threats.description: The load-bearing historical break: attacker-controlled input from the public context endpoint reaching OGNL/MVEL expression evaluation that can instantiate or call arbitrary Java, as in CVE-2020-11975, CVE-2020-13942, and CVE-2021-31164, fixed by constraining the public surface. A regression of this class is treated as valid and critical; the standing invariant is that no code execution is possible from public/untrusted input.

threats.name: Bypass of JSON-Schema event validation
threats.description: An unvalidated or unknown event shape reaches processing despite the registered JSON Schemas that should reject non-conforming input at the public boundary. Violates the input-validation property; severity security-critical to moderate.

threats.name: Cross-profile or cross-scope data access
threats.description: A public client reads or modifies profile data outside what the context/scope model permits, or an authenticated API client exceeds its authority (including the open tenant-isolation question UNOMI-139: whether a client with credentials for tenant A can reach tenant B's profiles, segments, or rules). Security-critical PII exposure.

threats.name: Resource exhaustion via public event floods
threats.description: A flood of events, large payloads, or expensive segments/conditions exhausts the server. The model leaves the resource-bound line unspecified (whether this is a bug or expected-and-operator-managed is an open maintainer question); the draft recommends rate limiting or a CDN/WAF in front of the public endpoint.

threats.name: Dangerous conditions authored by a trusted admin
threats.description: An authenticated privileged user defining server-side logic through conditions/rules is the intended (if powerful) feature, not an attack on Unomi; the expression/scripting allow-list protects the public surface and is not a sandbox that makes arbitrary admin-authored expressions safe. Out of model as trusted input.

threats.name: Admin APIs exposed unauthenticated or with default credentials
threats.description: Keeping the admin REST/GraphQL surface off the public network, authenticated, and free of default credentials is the operator's job (pending the draft's insecure-default ruling on whether a default-credential report is valid or a documented must-configure).

threats.name: Exposed or unsecured Elasticsearch/OpenSearch backend
threats.description: Unomi assumes a secured backend and does not defend an exposed Elasticsearch/OpenSearch or its network; confidentiality of profile data at rest in the search backend is deployment hardening, the operator's responsibility. A backend finding is in model only if reachable through Unomi's API.

threats.name: Corruption of analytics/segmentation by adversarial event injection
threats.description: Unomi does not guarantee correctness of analytics or segmentation under adversarial event injection beyond the access-control boundary; injected but schema-valid events skewing segments is a disclaimed property.

trustBoundaries.name: Public context endpoint boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Event payloads arrive unauthenticated from browsers and are untrusted; they flow through JSON-Schema validation, event/condition processing, and profile update to persistence. The schema-validation step and the public-event allow-list are the gate, not authentication; the endpoint being unauthenticated is by design.

trustBoundaries.name: Admin API boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The authenticated REST/GraphQL surface where conditions, rules, and scopes are defined; trusted to the credential, and expression power available only to a trusted authenticated author is out of model.

trustBoundaries.name: Persistence boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Unomi talks to an Elasticsearch/OpenSearch backend assumed trusted and operator-secured; findings on the backend are in model only when reachable through Unomi's API.

controls.name: JSON-Schema validation of incoming events
controls.description: Incoming events are validated against registered JSON Schemas so non-conforming input is rejected rather than processed; the intended primary input defense at the public boundary. Keep it enabled and register schemas for the events you accept (default strictness is an open maintainer question in the draft).

controls.name: Public-event allow-list and third-party server keys
controls.description: The protected-events / third-party server key mechanism (server id, key, IP allow-list, allowed-event-types configuration) distinguishes events a public client may send from those requiring a trusted key; keep it enabled rather than disabling it to ease integration.

controls.name: Expression/scripting restrictions on the public surface
controls.description: The post-CVE restrictions constrain which classes and methods condition expressions may reference so that public input cannot reach arbitrary OGNL/MVEL evaluation; they protect the public surface and are not a sandbox for admin-authored expressions.

controls.name: Keep admin APIs private and authenticated
controls.description: Keep the admin REST/GraphQL APIs off the public network and authenticated, and change any default credentials.

controls.name: Restrict condition/rule/scripting authoring authority
controls.description: Restrict who holds condition, rule, and scripting authoring authority: it is equivalent to server-side code definition.

controls.name: Secure the search backend and its network
controls.description: Secure the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch backend and the network between Unomi and it; do not expose the backend alongside Unomi without backend authentication.

controls.name: Rate limiting / CDN / WAF in front of the public endpoint
controls.description: Put the public context endpoint behind rate limiting or a CDN/WAF appropriate to public exposure, since flood protection may fall to the operator.
